## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them. `get` always lower-cases, so any value set under a mixed-case key can never be read back. This needs fixing before merge. The `DEFAULT_TTL` change and its comment match, and the expiry test is sound.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` using the key exactly as given, but `get` (app/cache.py:17) reads `self._store.get(key.lower())`. This breaks the rule in the comment at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together". For example, `c.set("Alpha", 1)` stores the key `"Alpha"`, and both `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` look up `"alpha"` and return `None`. The new test at tests/test_cache.py:12 only sets the lowercase key `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. Could you change line 27 to `self._store[key.lower()] = ...` and add a round-trip test that sets a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"`? — Callers moving from `_store` to `set` get permanent cache misses for any key that isn't all lowercase. Those entries also stay in `_store` forever, because the expiry delete in `get` only runs when the lookup finds the entry.

## Strengths
- The comment at app/cache.py:7 ("Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.") matches `DEFAULT_TTL = 300`, and the test at tests/test_cache.py:17-18 pins that value.
- `test_entries_expire` (tests/test_cache.py:21-27) makes expiry deterministic by monkeypatching `time.monotonic`. The patch takes effect because `cache.py` looks up `time.monotonic` through the module at call time.
